updates.name: Kim Miller
updates.bio: Manager of the Apalachicola National Estuarine Research Reserve, succeeding Jenna Harper, as reported by the Apalachicola Times in March 2025. Her 24 years with Florida DEP and the reserve include research, stewardship coordinator and aquatic preserve manager posts, most recently assistant manager. She holds a biology degree and has experience in estuarine ecology, restoration and coastal resource management.
updates.research_interests: coastal resource management; restoration; estuarine ecology
updates.current_affiliation: Apalachicola National Estuarine Research Reserve, Florida Department of Environmental Protection
updates.evidence: Succeeding her in the manager post at ANERR is Kim Miller
updates.notes: Bio source is an Apalachicola Times news story (2025-03-18) on her appointment; the page uses 'she'. status_source_url https://floridadep.gov/rcp/nerr-apalachicola redirects (200) to the floridaaquaticpreserves.org Apalachicola NERR page, which names Kim Miller as the reserve contact; it is a program page, not a personal homepage, so homepage_url left null. Verifier 2 (2026-10-26): bio no longer dates the appointment itself to March 2025 (the story is dated then but gives no appointment date). All cited pages re-fetched 200.

updates.name: F. Stuart Chapin III
updates.bio: Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Ecology based at the University of Alaska Fairbanks' Institute of Arctic Biology. His research centers on the Arctic, where tundra, permafrost and boreal forest face climate change, and on Earth Stewardship, which joins ecology with ethics. He works with Indigenous and local communities in Alaska and Siberia and received the 2019 Volvo Environment Prize.
updates.research_interests: climate and wildfire effects on Alaskan ecosystems and rural communities; sustainability and resilience of social-ecological systems; Earth stewardship; arctic and boreal ecology
updates.current_affiliation: Institute of Arctic Biology, University of Alaska Fairbanks

updates.name: Tessa M. Hill
updates.bio: Professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences at UC Davis and Bodega Marine Laboratory, formerly an associate vice provost for public scholarship and engagement. She studies past and present climate change and how marine species respond, including ocean acidification effects on Northern California shellfish growers, and is a fellow of AAAS and the California Academy of Sciences.
updates.research_interests: ocean acidification and coastal carbon flux; seagrass habitats and blue carbon; aquaculture farms as potential carbon storage; coastal climate archives from foraminifera and bivalves; paleoecology for conservation of species such as the Olympia oyster
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Earth & Planetary Sciences and Bodega Marine Laboratory, UC Davis

updates.name: Christa Mulder
updates.bio: Professor of Ecology in the Department of Biology and Wildlife and the Institute of Arctic Biology at the University of Alaska Fairbanks. A plant ecologist spanning population, community and ecosystem scales, she studies how species interact with one another and with their physical setting, drawing on field and greenhouse experiments, observational records and historical herbarium data.
updates.research_interests: climate change impacts on Arctic and subarctic plant communities and on the herbivores and pollinators that use them; spread of non-native plants across Interior Alaska; broadening participation in citizen science; Alaska berry futures
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Biology and Wildlife & Institute of Arctic Biology, University of Alaska Fairbanks
